about: Andrey's Y-structures and extended Y-structures against the authors' code on the datasets of the authors' simulation script, with and without selection; the release summary's Y-structures entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with the dependence check on claimed pairs and exact upper-tail p-values as merged)
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey and the authors' code ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: per cell (setting, with or without selection, form; 20 datasets of 10,000 rows from the authors' simulation script): per dataset, claim_error and claim_ap_loss; D = Andrey's minus the authors' code's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure is rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 is not rerun. The floor: claim_error minus the empty answer's, applied where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, passed when Andrey's interval lies wholly below 0; every row also gives the precision floor, passed when the pooled precision exceeds the pooled base rate with its 95% interval above 0
error_metric: claim_error: per dataset, the claimed ancestral pairs that are false plus the true ancestral pairs not claimed, among the system variables; claim_ap_loss: 1 minus the average precision of the ranking by the claims' scores, the pairs not claimed last. The floor uses claim_error against the empty answer's, the number of true pairs, so their difference is the false claims minus the true ones. precision_floor is the precision of the pooled claims minus the pooled base rate, the precision of claiming every pair
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one untimed warm-up fit before the timed one, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. Fisher's z tests at alpha 0.01, the level of the authors' script
seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a rerun holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: setting x dataset kind x form: fixed is the 7-node graph of the paper's Figure 5(a); small and large are random graphs with 8 and 16 system variables and a context variable (d counts the context); biased datasets keep the rows whose selection sum lies in [2, 2.5], unbiased datasets keep every row
comparisons_note: judged: rule authors, the selection variables drawn as the authors' simulation script draws them; the rule text, the selection variables among the leaves below the colliders as the paper's text describes them, is a harder setting reported as context and never judged
